valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 27 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a Sri Lankan commercial bank with branches in Bangladesh and a Maldives subsidiary; the bank earned Rs 49.5bn of the group's Rs 52.2bn nine-month profit (CBC Finance and other subsidiaries the rest), so one sector beta. (2)–(3) A bank, so no relevering: the sector's levered beta, Damodaran's Bank (Money Center) 0.70 (January 2026, as used for SAMP, HNB and NDB; web-search extract, his site couldn't be opened from this run). (4) Local betas from a web search (27 Nov 2026; pages not opened): StockAnalysis 0.69 (5-year), TradingView 1.06 (window not stated), Simply Wall St 0.97 (December 2024, window not stated); median 0.97. The voting share trades daily, so not thin. The annual report doesn't publish a beta. (5) Higher of 0.70 and 0.97 = 0.97. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and three verified local 5-year betas (only StockAnalysis states a 5-year window; on it alone the beta would be 0.70 and the cost of equity about 15.4%).

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (27 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.97 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.2%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 20 / 18 / 16.5% of the first analysis; the base is almost unchanged.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 7% / 10% / 12%; supported 14% (share of profit kept × ROE, FY 2025: 71.5% × 19.6%). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY 2025 figures; profit and dividend growth for the next five years. The 'kept' share counts the Rs 2.50 scrip dividend as paid out, although it stays in the bank as capital.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Unchanged. Group ROE 19.61% (2025), 21.96% (2024; 16.59% normalised for the debt restructuring), 18.6% for the twelve months to September 2026 (worked out by scripts/derived.py from the income statements and equity); bank ROE 9.78–14.66% in 2021–2023. The bank's own goal is over 20%. The base sits between the crisis years and the last three.

valuationInputs.name: ROE path (residual income)
valuationInputs.reason: Starts at the trailing twelve-month group ROE to 30 Sep 2026 (18.62%, ttm.roe from scripts/derived.py) and moves in a straight line to the long-run ROE over 10 years; then the excess return grows at the long-run rate. Payout 28% (the 'Dividends' input).

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Unchanged. Below the 12.24% bond yield and the cost of equity; needs 26–37% of profit kept (growth ÷ ROE).

valuationInputs.name: 2027 EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: Group EPS: Rs 36.86 (2025), Rs 31.08 for nine months of 2026 (+7%), trailing Rs 38.89; run-rate Rs 42.92 (Q1 2026 × 4). 2027: bear 3% above the trailing figure (impairments stay high, margins squeezed by deposit costs), base +10% on 2026's likely ~Rs 41, bull +20% (loan growth of 27% a year carries through). Base is 5% above the run-rate. P/Es within the bank's 2021–2025 year-end range (3.9–5.6x on the printed figures, 3–6x in the ten-year table) and at or below the justified 4.8x / 5.6x / 7.0x.

valuationInputs.name: Dividends
valuationInputs.value: Next year Rs 11.0 / 12.5 / 14.0 (about 28% of 2027 EPS), growing 7% / 10% / 12% for five years, then 5% / 6% / 7%
valuationInputs.reason: Rs 10.50 for 2025 (Rs 8.00 cash + Rs 2.50 in shares) was 28.5% of group EPS (bank's printed total payout 29%, cash 22%). After the five growth years the payout becomes 1 − long-run growth ÷ ROE (Damodaran's two-stage model): 66.7% / 64.7% / 63.2%, using the '2027 EPS × P/E' EPS and the 'Long-run ROE'. Growth is capped below the 14% supported. The scrip part is counted as a dividend.

openQuestions: Full-year 2026 (due February 2027): profit growth (nine months +8.6%), and the dividend: how much in cash and how much in shares.
Impairments: Rs 16.6bn in nine months (+18%), most of it in Q2 (Rs 11.7bn) as a buffer for 'external pressures'; does Q4 or 2027 bring a second wave as the 27% loan growth seasons?
Capital: CET1 12.50% and total capital 16.35% (minimum 14%) after loans grew Rs 348bn in nine months; any further Tier 2 issues, a larger scrip dividend or a rights issue.
Net interest margin (4.45%, from 4.51%) as deposit costs rise with interest rates.
ESOP-2026: up to 3% more voting shares (46.2m).
SLIC holdings: the Life Fund account fell from 77.9m to 12.0m shares while a new SLIC Life participating portfolio holds 63.3m; confirm it is an internal transfer.
Beta: recheck in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets bank beta and three verified local 5-year betas (only one source states a 5-year window).
Promises: bank ROE over 20% and profit growth over 20% (missed in 2025 and so far in 2026); OneApp launch in 2026; green portfolio towards Rs 100bn by 2030.

changeLog.summary: First analysis. Justified P/B, P/E, dividends and residual income; business tests 4 of 4 (category 2, watch list).

Requested from Telegram (/redo COMB.N0000 full). Research record rebuilt from the four CSE reports (annual report 2025 and interims to March, June and September 2026) as report figures only, with comparative columns as their own periods; earlier reportsRead kept, localFolder set to null. Cost of equity now from the house formula (beta 0.97, provisional: 18.2%); all four methods worked by scripts/valuation.py, with the dividend model on Damodaran's two-stage stable payout (it was well below the others before). NAV rose to Rs 224.63 and 2027 EPS assumptions to Rs 40 / 45 / 49 on the September results. Added management (plans and promises vs delivery) and shareholders. Business tests 4 of 4; category 2 (watch list), unchanged.
